rule.description: Workflow action-input reads must be confined to a single production module; every additional production module reading workflow inputs directly at its point of use is a scattered fragment of the same deployment-configuration responsibility, so a conceptual change to an input requires coordinated shotgun edits.

checks.description: Detects a production module reading a workflow action input directly at its point of use (core.getInput, its named-import/aliased/destructured equivalents, or its boolean/multiline variants) instead of consuming the single input-owner module's typed inputs contract.
checks.detected_relation: pipeline subsystem -> direct workflow action-input read bypassing the input-owner module
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The repository's design parses every workflow input once in one module and passes a typed inputs object through the pipeline. When each subsystem also re-reads and re-parses inputs locally, the same conceptual change to any input (rename, default, parsing convention, or semantic fix) must be repeated across orchestration, credential, preparation, and publish modules - the defining shotgun-surgery signature.

matches.evidence: run re-reads 'github_token' via core.getInput to evaluate fork-token availability instead of using the typed inputs object.
run re-reads 'deploy_key' via core.getInput for the same fork-skip decision.
run re-reads 'personal_token' via core.getInput for the same fork-skip decision.
run re-reads 'enable_jekyll' through an inline copy of the boolean parsing policy to re-derive the Jekyll decision.
run re-reads 'disable_nojekyll' with the same duplicated inline boolean coercion.
setTokens re-reads 'deploy_key' to pick the SSH auth method instead of trusting the typed inputs contract.
setTokens re-reads 'github_token' for the token auth dispatch branch.
setTokens re-reads 'personal_token' for the personal-token dispatch branch.
setSSHKey re-reads the raw 'deploy_key' secret to write the SSH key file instead of consuming the key material from the typed inputs.
setRepo re-reads 'publish_dir' to resolve the publish directory and workspace join itself.
setRepo re-reads 'destination_dir' and repeats the relative-path check locally.
setRepo re-reads 'publish_branch' to pick the clone and orphan-branch target.
setRepo re-reads 'force_orphan' through the local boolean-coercion copy.
setRepo re-reads 'keep_files' to decide whether existing files are kept.
setRepo re-reads 'exclude_assets' to build the exclusion list for asset copying.
commit re-reads 'allow_empty_commit' and ignores its typed parameter to decide --allow-empty.
push re-reads 'publish_branch' to determine the push target, leaving its branch argument unused.
push re-reads 'force_orphan' through the local boolean-coercion copy to decide --force.
pushTag re-reads 'tag_name' to choose the annotated tag, leaving its tagName argument unused.
pushTag re-reads 'tag_message' and locally re-implements the 'Deployment <tag>' default.

excluded.what: The 20 input reads inside the input-owner module (src/get-inputs.ts, getInputs)
excluded.why: These are the healthy single-owner reads that parse the workflow inputs into the typed inputs object. The rule deliberately treats a set of reads confined to one module as the repaired state, so these sites are not smell matches; in the injected output they are listed for transparency only.

excluded.what: core.getInput calls in unit tests would be outside production scope, and the checker analyzes src/** only
excluded.why: Private test scaffolding is not a production responsibility owner and never counts toward the module count.
